faqs.a: 16 or more characters for important accounts like email and banking; the slider goes up to 64. Length adds strength faster than exotic symbols do.
faqs.q: How long should my password be?

faqs.a: Bits of unpredictability. Each extra bit doubles the cracking effort: 60 bits is fair, 80 bits is good, and 100+ bits is effectively uncrackable by brute force today.
Yes. Passwords come from crypto.getRandomValues, the browser's cryptographic random generator — not from a predictable pseudo-random formula.
Do it when humans will read or type the password — I, l, 1, O and 0 are easy to confuse. It shrinks the character pool slightly, which costs a little entropy.
No — never reuse passwords. A breach on one site would hand attackers the keys to every other account sharing that password.
faqs.q: Can I reuse a generated password on two sites?

faqs.a: Never. Generation happens locally on your device; nothing is transmitted, logged or stored. Copy your password before leaving the page.

password-generator.formula: entropy (bits) = password length x log2(character pool size). Example: 16 characters drawn from 87 possible characters gives 16 x 6.44 = about 103 bits. The average number of guesses to crack it is 2^(bits - 1); at 10 billion guesses per second, 103 bits would take far longer than the age of the universe.
howTo: Drag the slider to set a length — 16 is a solid default.

Strength is measured in bits of entropy: length x log2(character pool).

Longer beats 'complex': a 20-character simple password outruns an 8-character tricky one.
A generated password exists only on this page until you copy it.
limitations: Crack-time estimates assume a fixed attacker speed of 10 billion guesses per second — real attacks vary.
A strong password cannot protect a breached or phishing site — use a password manager and unique passwords per site.
